A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIRROR research work. All 26 pages of each version, including appendix text, tables, diagrams, examples, and evaluator instructions, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulated counseling evaluations, expert pairwise assessments, response-length analyses, and counseling case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains the original automated evaluations, expert assessments, and supplementary empirical analyses.

M1.justification: V2 gives emotional captioning a standalone Section 4, but its image-to-caption-to-response procedure already appears in v1 Section 4.2, Appendix C, and the unchanged prompts. Dataset construction, planning, and model training remain the same. Changing 'five' quality filters to 'six' corrects a miscount of filters already listed in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIRROR constructed from CelebA and CACTUS, simulated resistant and non-resistant clients, and AnnoMI counseling demonstrations. No dataset, resistance category, or evaluated task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain LLAMA-3-8B, CAMEL-LLAMA3, GPT-3.5-TURBO, and LLAVA-V1.5-7B as comparators. The expert study retains LLAMA-3-8B and CAMEL-LLAMA3. V2 adds a rationale for selecting these expert-study baselines without changing participation.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain unchanged: 600 resistant and 200 non-resistant evaluation profiles, the same client simulator and stopping rule, identical assessment scales, and expert comparisons using 200 selected cases. Training settings and evaluator instructions also match.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the planning/captioning comparisons, response-length correlations, failure analyses, virtual and AnnoMI case studies, and stage-direction comparison. Their relocation and the new limitations discussion do not establish additional analyses.

E5.justification: The paired t-test reporting at p < 0.05 and correlation-significance captions are unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or another uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–6 and the empirical plots are unchanged. V2 Section 6.3 newly reports expert feedback that goal pursuit occurred implicitly through sustained rapport and motivational alignment; v1 reports the preference results without this qualitative account.

T1.justification: Neither version contains a formal theoretical contribution or proofs. The conceptual assessment categories and methodological descriptions introduce no changed mathematical definitions, assumptions, or derivations.

C1.justification: V1 presents emotional captioning as an explored CoT strategy; v2 explicitly presents it as a proposed novel reasoning contribution in the introduction and contribution list. The central claims about MIRROR and multimodal management of client resistance remain.

C2.justification: V2 replaces v1's description of broadly consistent Goal scores with an explanation of lower scores against some baselines as a tradeoff from prioritizing emotional engagement. It also adds a specific limitation concerning prolonged supportive dialogue without therapeutic progress and insufficient session structure.

D1.justification: V2 removes the direct Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct checkpoint link supplied in v1 Section 3.3, although Figure 2 retains the model identifier. Training hyperparameters, hardware, prompts, model-version information, and release/licensing disclosures otherwise remain available.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wang et al. (2025) to support the discussion of text-based CBT limitations. The related-work discussion moves largely unchanged to Appendix B. Updating Kim et al. (2025) from its preprint to its conference publication does not introduce another work.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the introduction, dataset-construction explanation, and experimental exposition. It reorganizes the contributions, establishes a separate emotional-captioning section, and moves related work from the main text to Appendix B, materially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 restyles Figure 1 and the planning/captioning diagrams, replacing client emojis with facial images in the latter. The captioning diagram moves into the main text; table headings, evaluator instructions, and several figure/table placements change. Empirical graphics retain their content.

improvement.justification: V2 explains the existing dataset construction and captioning workflow more clearly and adds a concrete limitation about dialogue continuing without therapeutic progress. These provide a limited improvement in clarity and qualification. Numerical evidence and validation coverage remain unchanged, and the new rapport-based explanation is not separately tested; removal of one checkpoint link slightly reduces access guidance.
